The user is asking for onboarding copy for a Traditional Chinese expense tracking app. They want three onboarding pages, each with a title (t1, t2, t3) and subtitle (b1, b2, b3), plus a CTA button (cta). They explicitly asked to return only JSON in the specified format.

Key requirements:
1. Traditional Chinese (繁體中文)
2. Page 1: Connect bank accounts for automatic transaction import
3. Page 2: Automatic expense categorization
4. Page 3: Monthly budget reminders
5. Last page has a "Get Started" button
6. Return ONLY JSON in the format: {"t1":"...","b1":"...","t2":"...","b2":"...","t3":"...","b3":"...","cta":"..."}

They explicitly said "只回傳 JSON" (only return JSON). So I should not include any explanation, just the JSON itself.

Let me craft good copy:

Page 1: 連結銀行帳戶自動匯入交易
- Title: Something catchy about linking bank accounts
- e.g., 「一鍵連結您的銀行帳戶」 or 「連結銀行帳戶」
- Subtitle: explaining automatic import of transactions

Page 2: 自動分類支出
- Title: about automatic categorization
- Subtitle: explaining no more manual categorization

Page 3: 每月預算提醒
- Title: about budget reminders
- Subtitle: about staying on track
- CTA: 「開始使用」

Let me write compelling Traditional Chinese copy:

t1: 連結銀行帳戶
b1: 自動匯入交易明細，記帳從此不用手動輸入

t2: 支出自動分類
b2: AI 智慧辨識每筆消費，輕鬆掌握金錢流向

Hmm, should I mention AI? The requirement says automatic categorization. Maybe keep it simple:

t2: 自動分類支出
b2: 每筆交易自動歸類，支出流向一目瞭然

t3: 掌握每月預算
b3: 即時預算提醒，幫您守住每個月的錢包

cta: 開始使用

Let me refine:

t1: 連結銀行帳戶，交易自動匯入
b1: 只要連結一次，所有消費明細自動同步，告別手動記帳

Maybe shorter titles are better for onboarding screens:

t1: 連結您的銀行帳戶
b1: 自動匯入交易明細，記帳不再需要手動輸入

t2: 支出自動分類

t3: 每月預算提醒
b3: 接近預算上限即時通知，輕鬆守住每月開銷

cta: 開始使用

These look good. The user asked to return ONLY JSON, so my response should be just the JSON object, no additional text, no markdown code fences probably. Actually, should I use code fences? The instruction says "只回傳 JSON" — for a programmatic use case, raw JSON is likely parsed. Code fences could break parsing. Best to return just the raw JSON.

Format considerations: Should it be pretty-printed or single line? The example format they gave is single-line-ish. I'll return it in the exact structure they specified. A single-line JSON matches their template exactly. I could also format it with line breaks for readability, but since they gave an inline example and it's likely for parsing, I'll match their format — inline JSON.

Final:

{"t1":"連結您的銀行帳戶","b1":"自動匯入交易明細，記帳不再需要手動輸入","t2":"支出自動分類","b2":"智慧辨識每筆消費，金錢流向一目瞭然","t3":"每月預算提醒","b3":"接近預算上限即時通知，輕鬆守住每月開銷","cta":"開始使用"}

Check: Traditional Chinese characters — yes all traditional (帳戶, 進, 輸, 響, 瞭, 額, 鬆, 開, 守). Good.
